overall: The committee did not violate the law by failing to announce recordings because the chair was not told of them, but a committee member individually violated it by emailing a quorum about public business; the AG declined the untimely and non-OML claims.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee violated the law by recording its October 30 and November 1, 2012 meetings without first notifying the chair or participants.
Complaint alleged a committee member deliberated by email with a quorum of the committee on the recording issue in November and December 2012, outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Expression of an opinion on matters within a body's jurisdiction to a quorum of a public body is a deliberation, even if no other public body member responds.

allegations.summary: Complaint challenged June 22 and November 2, 2012 emails, which were untimely because the complainant was copied on them when sent.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore decline to review the allegations regarding the June 22, 2012 and November 2, 2012 emails, as they are untimely.

allegations.summary: Complaint also alleged a violation of G.L. c. 272, § 99 (interception of oral communications), which is outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: This determination concerns only the enforcement of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25; therefore we decline to review this allegation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution Mr. Zachmann that future similar conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
